synopsis: ISO 18571 objectively rates agreement between two time signals, combining corridor, phase, magnitude and slope sub-scores into a single “ISO score”; an example comparison is measured versus simulated deceleration for the same run [f14744, f15331, f15332]. An IDIADA and MathWorks demonstration recorded on 14 April 2026 used ISO 18571 to correlate a closed-loop virtual AEB setup—virtual sensors, vehicle dynamics and controller—against production-vehicle proving-ground tests [f1269, f1762]. The glossary identifies this as the kind of correlation metric needed when simulation is presented in the Euro NCAP manner [f15341]. The cited application is on-road, and the supplied facts report neither achieved scores nor acceptance thresholds or heavy off-road validation results [f1269, f15331]. CORA is described as an older, structurally similar crash-safety rating method, but only as background rather than a method mentioned in the booklet [f14747].
